module.open_ports.checks: Tests a list of common TCP ports on the target address and reports exposed sensitive services (databases, remote access, file sharing).
module.open_ports.fix:
Close right away the sensitive ports listed (database, remote access, file sharing, administration API) that have no reason to be reachable from the Internet: a blocking rule in the hosting provider's firewall (security group, network firewall) AND in the server's own firewall.
If a sensitive service was reachable without protection, treat it as compromised: change its passwords and keys, read its logs and look for unknown accounts, scheduled tasks or containers.
Apply the rule "deny everything inbound, except what is needed": open to the public only `80` and `443` (plus `25`, `465`, `587` and `993` only on a mail server), on IPv6 as well as IPv4.
Administration (SSH `22`, RDP `3389`, VNC `5900`, WinRM `5985` and `5986`): allow only the administrator's fixed address, or go through a VPN or a jump host; never expose RDP or VNC directly to the Internet.
Databases and caches (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle, Redis, MongoDB, Elasticsearch, Memcached, CouchDB): make them listen on `127.0.0.1` or on the private network (`bind-address` for MySQL, `listen_addresses` for PostgreSQL, `bind` for Redis, `network.host` for Elasticsearch, `bindIp` for MongoDB) and require a password.
Windows RPC and file sharing (`135`, `139`, `445`) and NFS (`2049`): block them at the network edge, they never need to be public.
Docker: a port published with `-p 6379:6379` can bypass ufw rules; publish on the local address (`-p 127.0.0.1:6379:6379`) and never expose the Docker API (`2375`), which gives control of the machine.
Test or administration interfaces (Grafana `3000`, GlassFish `4848`, WebLogic `7001`, Consul `8500`): put them behind a VPN or a reverse proxy with authentication, or disable them if they are no longer used.
Check from outside the network (not from the server): `nmap -Pn -p 22,3306,3389 203.0.113.10` must show `filtered` or `closed` (also in IPv6 with `nmap -6`), then rerun the port scan.
module.open_ports.fix_snippet:
# ufw
sudo ufw default deny incoming
sudo ufw allow 80/tcp
sudo ufw allow 443/tcp
sudo ufw allow from 203.0.113.10 to any port 22 proto tcp
sudo ufw enable
sudo ufw status numbered

# firewalld
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --remove-port=3306/tcp
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --remove-service=mysql
sudo firewall-cmd --reload
sudo firewall-cmd --list-all

# PowerShell
Get-NetFirewallPortFilter | Where-Object { $_.LocalPort -eq 3389 } | Get-NetFirewallRule | Set-NetFirewallRule -Enabled False
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "RDP admin only" -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 3389 -RemoteAddress 203.0.113.10 -Action Allow

# Docker Compose
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:16
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432"
module.open_ports.title: Open ports
module.open_ports.why: An administration service or database reachable from the Internet is one of the first targets of automated attacks.
